claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate resistance to oxygen attack or pesting.
An anti-oxidation coating is required for high-temperature use of this alloy family in air.
A thin aluminum-rich aluminide diffusion coating can be applied by pack cementation or chemical vapor deposition.
Applying a thin aluminide diffusion coating will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide coating will produce a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The aluminide coating will diffuse into the substrate and form a thin intermetallic surface layer.
Oxidation of the intermetallic surface layer will form a slow-growing protective alumina scale.
The alumina scale will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier and reduce oxygen ingress and pesting.
The thin coating and oxide scale will leave the bulk alloy microstructure largely intact.
Relative to uncoated material, coated specimens will exhibit reduced or delayed pesting after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
The room-temperature ductility of coated specimens will remain comparable to that of uncoated specimens.
The 1000 °C yield strength of coated specimens at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 will remain comparable to that of uncoated specimens.
Air exposure at 800 °C for 5 hours and subsequent tensile testing reproduce the relevant baseline conditions.
